##Simple linear regression
```{r}
data("women")
fit<-lm(weight~height, data=women)
summary(fit)
```

```{r}
women$weight
```
##extracting the fitted values from a model object

```{r}
fitted(fit)
```

#Observed minus fitted(error)

```{r}
residuals(fit)
```

```{r}
plot(women$height,women$weight,xlab="Height (in inches)",ylab="Weight (in pounds)")
abline(fit)
```

##The plot suggests that you might be able to improve on the prediction by using a line with one bend. WE can fit the polynomial regression.
# Polynomial regression

```{r}
fit2<- lm(weight~height+I(height^2), data=women)
summary(fit2)
```

```{r}
plot(women$height,women$weight,xlab="Height (in inches)",ylab="Weight (in pounds)")
lines(women$height,fitted(fit2))
```

##Multiple regresion model
```{r}
View(longley)
head(longley)
tail(longley)
str(longley)
```
#Summary statistics of Longley dataset
```{r}
summary(longley)
```

##Fitting model
```{r}
fit <- lm(Employed ~ GNP + Unemployed + Armed.Forces + Population,
          data = longley)
summary(fit)
```
#Using all other columns as predictors
```{r}
fit_all <- lm(Employed ~ ., data = longley)
summary(fit_all)
```

#Useful follow-up

```{r}
coef(fit)
confint(fit)
fitted(fit)
resid(fit)
anova(fit)

predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(GNP = 400,
                                  Unemployed = 300,
                                  Armed.Forces = 250,
                                  Population = 120))
```
#Checking multicollinearity
```{r}
cor(longley)          # many correlations near 0.9 or higher
```

#Diagnostic plots
```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(fit)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

#Comparing models
```{r}
fit1 <- lm(Employed ~ GNP, data = longley)
fit2 <- lm(Employed ~ GNP + Unemployed + Armed.Forces, data = longley)

anova(fit1, fit2)     # does adding predictors improve the fit?
AIC(fit1, fit2)       # lower is better
```
```{r}
install.packages("car")
library(car)
```

#A simpler model that drops redundant predictors
```{r}
fit_small <- lm(Employed ~ GNP + Unemployed + Armed.Forces, data = longley)
summary(fit_small)
vif(fit_small)
```

#Plot fitted vs actual
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data.frame(actual = longley$Employed, fitted = fitted(fit)),
       aes(x = fitted, y = actual)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_abline(color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Longley: Actual vs Fitted Employment",
       x = "Fitted", y = "Actual") +
  theme_minimal()
```

##Variable selection methods

```{r}
install.packages(c("MASS", "leaps", "glmnet", "caret", "car", "randomForest"))
```

#Filter methods
```{r}
data(mtcars)

# Correlation with the response
cor(mtcars)[, "mpg"]

# Univariate test for one predictor
summary(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars))

# Multicollinearity: VIF (values above about 5-10 are a concern)
library(car)
full <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
vif(full)

# Near-zero variance variables
library(caret)
nearZeroVar(mtcars, names = TRUE)
```

#Wrapper methods
```{r}
library(MASS)

null <- lm(mpg ~ 1, data = mtcars)
full <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)

# Forward
fwd <- stepAIC(null, scope = list(lower = null, upper = full),
               direction = "forward")

# Backward
bwd <- stepAIC(full, direction = "backward")

# Both directions
both <- stepAIC(full, direction = "both")

summary(both)
```

#Best subset selection
```{r}
library(leaps)

best <- regsubsets(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, nvmax = 10)
s <- summary(best)

# Compare sizes using different criteria
which.max(s$adjr2)   # adjusted R²
which.min(s$cp)      # Mallows' Cp
which.min(s$bic)     # BIC

# Coefficients of the best model by BIC
coef(best, which.min(s$bic))

# Plot
plot(best, scale = "bic")
```

#Recursive feature elimination
```{r}
library(caret)

ctrl <- rfeControl(functions = lmFuncs, method = "cv", number = 10)
rfe_fit <- rfe(x = mtcars[, -1], y = mtcars$mpg,
               sizes = 1:10, rfeControl = ctrl)

rfe_fit
predictors(rfe_fit)
```

#Embedded methods
```{r}
library(glmnet)

x <- model.matrix(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)[, -1]  # drop intercept column
y <- mtcars$mpg

set.seed(123)

# Lasso (alpha = 1), with cross-validation to choose lambda
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 1)
plot(cv_lasso)

cv_lasso$lambda.min   # lambda with lowest CV error
cv_lasso$lambda.1se   # simpler model within 1 SE of the best

# Selected variables (nonzero coefficients)
coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.1se")

# Ridge: alpha = 0
cv_ridge <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 0)

# Elastic net: alpha between 0 and 1
cv_enet <- cv.glmnet(x, y, alpha = 0.5)
```

#Random forest importance
```{r}
library(randomForest)

set.seed(123)
rf <- randomForest(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, importance = TRUE)

importance(rf)
varImpPlot(rf)
```

#Simulation a linear model

```{r}
## Always set your seed!
 set.seed(20)

 ## Simulate predictor variable
 x <- rnorm(100)

 ## Simulate the error term
 e <- rnorm(100, 0, 2)

 ## Compute the outcome via the model
 y <- 0.5 - 2 * x + e

plot(x, y)
```

```{r}
set.seed(1)
sample(1:10, 4)
```
